_comment: PDF-96 D2/D3. The six-layer spine, hand-authored and test-pinned by tests/test_website_diagrams.py against tests/test_import_boundaries.py's own AST walk and src/pdf_tooling/ports/__init__.py's PORTS tuple. Every count below is a derived fact, not a guess -- re-derive rather than hand-edit a number here. Corrects Architecture.astro's pre-PDF-96 rendering, which drew a seventh, invented 'Engines' layer and omitted output/ entirely.

layers.name: CLI
layers.rule: The only layer that may import the CLI framework.
layers.desc: Parses flags, builds one frozen OperationPlan, picks a renderer.

layers.name: Ops
layers.rule: Framework-free verbs, pure functions over ports — never a filesystem-tier refusal built locally.
layers.desc: No I/O except through Safety and Ports.
layers.forkNote: Ops reaches Safety and Ports in parallel.

layers.name: Safety
layers.rule: The single write chokepoint — one file, not one package. Both write allowlists are the empty set.
layers.desc: Write-to-temp, fsync, atomic rename. The --dry-run gate.

layers.name: Ports
layers.rule: typing.Protocol definitions only — importing every port module loads no engine.
layers.desc: The type contract nothing passes through.

layers.name: Adapters
layers.rule: The only package that may import an engine library. subprocess_util.py is the only module in the tree that may spawn a process.
layers.desc: Eight modules back the six ports above; the ninth file is the spawn chokepoint, not a port backer.

layers.name: Output
layers.rule: stdout is the payload; stderr is everything else.
layers.desc: What Ops returns, rendered as table, json or ndjson.

engines.name: Engines
engines.note: Not this codebase. Permissive licences only, checked in CI.

boundary.label: Enforced boundary
boundary.above: no engine import, no spawn, no write outside the chokepoint
